summary: Today’s pulse tracks UK children just as likely to have suffered harm on social media despite crackdown, As midterms loom, Trump and his allies try to change the subject, and White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are trump, children, and robinson. In the background, Melania Trump has helped broker ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town, says White House – Europe live and Trump’s justice department sues to block Senate race certification in Alaska if Republican loses – live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: UK children just as likely to have suffered harm on social media despite crackdown
headlines.description: Campaigners call lack of progress ‘staggering’, as Ofcom also admits little change in severity of harm to children encountering unsafe content Landmark online safety measures have failed to limit the proportion of children suffering harm from social media, the UK’s online regulator has admitted, in an assessment branded “staggering” by campaigners. The proportion of children being fed unsafe content that often left them frightened, confused and upset, was almost unchanged, according to an Ofcom review of the first nine months of supposedly strict requirements on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.

headlines.title: As midterms loom, Trump and his allies try to change the subject
headlines.description: Despite distraction and distortion, voters know what issues will be informing their votes in this election This was originally published in The Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox Elections too often get pigeonholed. The hot take, or simplistic analysis, would have it that just one issue – often the issue the source so happens to be most animated about – will decide the entire result. Tens of millions of Americans will go to the polls next month. Will they be galvanized by affordability? Maybe it’s Iran. Or healthcare? Taxes, perhaps. Or crime.

headlines.title: White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
headlines.description: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.

headlines.title: Melania Trump has helped broker ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town, says White House – Europe live
headlines.description: Residents in Oleshky have been enduring a worsening humanitarian crisis due to the lack of food, electricity and other resources The French prime minister Sébastien Lecornu has just issued a statement on a shooting in a town west of Paris this morning where one person was killed and four others injured. Police said a gunman had opened fire in Trappes, in the Yvelines, and neighbouring La Verriere. The gunman was later arrested in nearby Coignieres.

headlines.title: Trump’s justice department sues to block Senate race certification in Alaska if Republican loses – live
headlines.description: Preliminary lawsuit claims there could be ‘voter confusion’ about the two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, which could influence the race’s outcome in favor of the Democratic nominee, Mary Peltola They break down the final stretch ahead of these hugely consequential elections, that will decide control of Congress in Donald Trump’s final two years of office.

headlines.title: Tommy Robinson guilty of harassment because this is not a vigilante world, jury told
headlines.description: Prosecution says Robinson ‘threatened people and acted like a bully’ towards Daily Mail journalists Tommy Robinson is guilty of harassing two journalists because we do not live in a “vigilante world”, jurors have been told, as the prosecution sought to use the far-right activist’s words against him. Robinson had posted a video in which he told Daily Mail journalists he would find them after they wrote about his alleged role influencing England’s 2024 riots. He told them he had obtained details of where they and their families lived and warned them to abide by “men’s rules”.

headlinePool.title: Oil price rises above $117 a barrel amid fears US will renew strikes on Iran
headlinePool.description: Brent crude increase follows Tehran threatening retaliatory attacks on Gulf refineries and datacentres Oil has hit its highest level in more than six months as fears of fresh escalation in the Middle East conflict grip the energy markets. Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, rose by about 3.5% on Friday to pass $117 a barrel at one point – its highest level since April.

headlinePool.title: Reform braces for Farage standards verdict over undeclared £5m gift
headlinePool.description: Party insiders say they expect initial verdict to be against leader and are preparing to appeal against adverse findings Nigel Farage’s Reform is braced for a negative report from the standards commissioner over his failure to declare a £5m gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, and plans to appeal against any adverse findings. The party is on tenterhooks over the report, with multiple Reform insiders saying they are readying for a fightback through the appeals process and fully expect the initial verdict to find against him.

headlinePool.title: Officer who shot and killed Black toddler in Mississippi resigns from police force
headlinePool.description: Hunter Foster fired at vehicle during a shoplifting call at a Walmart, killing one-year-old Kohen Wiley Hunter Foster, the Mississippi police officer who shot into a vehicle and killed one-year-old Kohen Wiley, has resigned from the Senatobia police department. Earlier this week, Mississippi’s attorney general, Lynn Fitch, announced that the shooting was “justified”. The Senatobia board of aldermen accepted Foster’s resignation on 21 October and the resignation took effect immediately. Foster was placed on leave on 16 June, days after the 14 June shooting. Yesterday, the Mississippi department of public safety released body-camera and surveillance footage from the shooting, at a Walmart in Senatobia, during which the toddler died in his mother’s arms after being shot.

headlinePool.title: Opposition deepfake video sparks outrage in Spain ahead of election
headlinePool.description: Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing A political ad from Spain’s main opposition party that used a deepfake video of the prime minister’s wife has sparked outrage and set off a wider debate on AI, as the deeply polarised country gears up for general elections next month. Launched this week across the social media channels of the conservative People’s party (PP), the video used artificial intelligence to manipulate the likenesses of various people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party and appeared to show them admitting to acts such as soliciting prostitutes and taking kickbacks.

headlinePool.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
headlinePool.description: Thirty-four people are also injured in the attack in southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.

headlinePool.title: Thousands of homes without power as Storm Austen hits south-west England
headlinePool.description: Dozens of schools in Cornwall also affected as another storm heads for Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England Thousands of homes are without power and schools were closed as the first named storm of the year hit UK shores. Storm Austen brought severe conditions to parts of the south-west, with a gust of 76mph recorded at St Mary’s airport on the Isles of Scilly on Friday morning. Just before 11am, more than 16,000 homes in the south-west were without power, according to National Grid.

headlinePool.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
headlinePool.description: The network is used by the Ukrainian military, sources say, and Trump says "if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out".

headlinePool.title: Deadly shooting near Paris investigated as 'crime of terrorism', minister says
headlinePool.description: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks and the suspected gunman has been apprehended.

headlinePool.title: Which is really England’s oldest pub? Tree-ring dating helps settle debate
headlinePool.description: Historic England archaeologist says some inns’ claims to date back 1,000 years are inaccurate and oldest is from 1430 With their low ceilings, timber beams and roaring fires, many of England’s inns lay claim to being the oldest in the land and to have been visited by Vikings and Saxons. But an archaeologist working for Historic England says not one of the more than two dozen pubs that make this claim is being accurate.
